title: 考研英语二2025年真题及答案解析（整卷）

sentences.text: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage.
sentences.translation: 美国顾客历来会给那些他们认为主要靠小费谋生的人支付小费,比如收入低于最低工资的餐厅服务员。2010年代初,各类商家开始使用iPad和其他数字支付系统处理交易。这些系统经常提示顾客为以前不需要支付小费的服务支付小费。

sentences.text: In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems.
These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped.
Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip.
sentences.translation: 如今的小费要求往往与过去决定何时以及如何支付小费的薪资和服务规范脱节。过去顾客几乎总是在接受服务后支付小费,比如在用完餐后、理完发后或披萨送达后。这种时机可以奖励高质量的服务,并激励员工提供优质服务。

sentences.text: Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered.
That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.
It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand.
sentences.translation: 事先要求支付小费的情况正变得越来越普遍。而新的小费技术甚至可能自动添加小费。

sentences.text: And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.
Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers.
sentences.translation: 值得注意的是,小费主要惠及其中一些员工,如服务员,但不惠及其他员工,如厨师和洗碗工。为确保所有员工获得公平工资,一些餐厅禁止收小费并提高了价格,但这种取消小费服务的运动基本上已经失败。

sentences.text: To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.
So, to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation.
sentences.translation: 因此,为了在不提高价格的情况下增加员工工资,越来越多的雇主屈服于小费蔓延和小费通胀的诱惑。然而,许多顾客感到沮丧,因为他们觉得自己被要求支付过高的小费,而且频率过高。而且,正如我们的研究所强调的,小费现在似乎更具强制性、更缺乏慷慨性,并且往往与服务质量完全脱节。

sentences.text: However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often.
And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely dissociated from service quality.
Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed.
sentences.translation: 解决健康和护理危机的许多答案都已被反复讨论。我们需要在减少和分流医疗服务需求方面做得更好,而不是仅仅对其进行管理。需要在社区和基层医疗方面投入更多资金,以减少我们对医院的依赖。社会护理的能力需要更大,以支持日益增长的长期病患者数量。懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2025-english-two/section2-part-a-2/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好

sentences.text: We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it.
Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals.
And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions.
Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims.
sentences.translation: 然而,尽管经历了二十年的战略规划和多次重大卫生改革,我们在任何这些目标上都未能取得实质性进展。这就是为什么Reform智库在十位前卫生大臣的支持下启动了一项名为"重新构想健康"的新工作计划。我们共同呼吁就英国健康的未来进行更加开放和诚实的对话,并"紧急反思"我们所保留的以医院为中心的模式。

sentences.text: That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work entitled "Reimagining health", supported by ten former health ministers.
Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an "urgent rethink" of the hospital-centric model we retain.
Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years.
sentences.translation: 近年来，高温行动计划(HAPs)在印度迅速普及。一般来说，高温行动计划明确规定了官员应何时以及如何发布高温警报并提醒医院和其他机构。例如,那格浦尔的计划要求医院在夏季预留"降温病房"用于治疗中暑患者,并建议建筑商在酷热天气让建筑工人停工休息。

sentences.text: In general, an HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions.

Nagpur's plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside "cold wards" in the summer for treating heatstroke patients, and advises builders to give construction laborers a break from work on very hot days.
But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Centre for Policy Research.
sentences.translation: 但根据政策研究中心的一份报告,现有高温行动计划的实施情况参差不齐。报告发现,许多计划缺乏充足的资金。而且它们的触发阈值往往没有根据当地气候进行定制。在某些地区,仅白天的高温就可以作为发布警报的充分触发条件。但在其他地方,夜间温度或湿度可能与白天高温一样,都是风险的重要衡量指标。

sentences.text: Many lack adequate funding, it found.
And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate.
In some areas, high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts.
But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs.
To help improve HAPs, urban planner Rajashree Kotharkar's team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions.
sentences.translation: 为了帮助改进高温行动计划,城市规划师Rajashree Kotharkar的团队正在制定一个示范计划,概述最佳实践并可根据当地条件进行调整。她说,除其他事项外,所有城市都应该绘制脆弱性地图,以帮助将应对措施集中在风险最高的人群上。

sentences.text: Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk.
HAPs shouldn't just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say, but also recommend medium- to long-term measures that could make communities cooler.
sentences.translation: 研究人员表示,高温行动计划不应仅包括短期应急响应,还应推荐可使社区更凉爽的中长期措施。例如在那格浦尔,Kotharkar的团队已能够就在哪里种植树木以提供遮阴向市政官员提供建议。高温行动计划还可以指导房屋改造或修改建筑法规的工作。气候研究员Chandni Singh说:"在紧急情况下减少死亡是一个值得追求的目标,但这是最低目标。

sentences.text: In Nagpur, for example, Kotharkar's team has been able to advise city officials about where to plant trees to provide shade.
HAPs could also guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations.
"Reducing deaths in an emergency is a good target to have, but it's the lowest target," says climate researcher Chandni Singh.
Urban planners interpret desire paths as more than just convenient shortcuts; they offer valuable insights into the dynamics between planning and behaviour.
sentences.translation: 城市规划者将欲望路径解读为不仅仅是便捷的捷径;它们提供了关于规划与行为之间动态关系的宝贵见解。俄亥俄州立大学允许其学生自由穿行校园中心的椭圆形草坪,然后铺设这些欲望路径,创建了学生已经建立的有效路线网络。

sentences.text: Ohio State University allowed its students to navigate the Oval, a lawn in the centre of campus, freely, then proceeded to pave the desire paths, creating a web of effective routes students had established.
Yet, reluctance persists among other planners to integrate desire paths into formal plans, citing concerns about safety, environmental impact, or primarily, aesthetics.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2025-english-two/section2-part-a-4/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好user-driven evolution of public spaces and the desire for a visually curated and controlled urbanenvironment.然而,其他规划者仍然不愿将欲望路径纳入正式规划,理由是对安全、环境影响,或主要是美观的担忧。一个专门讨论这一现象的Reddit网页拥有近5万名成员,展示了当地欲望路径的图片,这些路径上装饰着指示行人遵守指定人行道的标志,凸显了这些人造小径固有的叛逆性质。这种冲突凸显了公共空间有机的、用户驱动的演变与对视觉上精心策划和控制的城市环境的渴望之间的持续斗争。

sentences.text: A Reddit webpage devoted to the phenomenon, boasting nearly 50,000 members, showcases images of local desire paths adorned with signs instructing pedestrians to adhere to designated walkways, underscoring the rebellious nature inherent in these human-made tracks.
This clash highlights an ongoing struggle between the organic,
In online spaces, desire paths have sparked a fascination that can approach obsession, with the Reddit page serving as a hub.
sentences.translation: 在网络空间中,欲望路径激发了一种可能接近痴迷的迷恋,Reddit页面成为一个中心。贡献者提供了各种各样的故事,从鲜为人知的新捷径到长期存在的替代路线。

sentences.text: Contributors offer a wide array of stories, from little-known new shortcuts to long-established alternate routes.
Animal desire paths, such as ducks forging trails through frozen ponds or dogs carving direct routes in gardens, highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences.
sentences.translation: 动物欲望路径,如鸭子在结冰的池塘上开辟小径或狗在花园中开辟直接路线,突显了这些小径在人类和动物体验中的适应性。随着欲望路径在物理和虚拟景观中纵横交错,它们证明了集体坚持开辟非常规路线和拥抱共同选择精神的决心。

sentences.text: As desire paths criss-cross through both physical and virtual landscapes, they stand as a proof of the collective insistence on forging unconventional routes and embracing the spirit of communal choice.

Researchers analysed the frequency and impact of gaps greater than 2 seconds during conversations, including an overview of previous studies which indicate that the fear of awkward silences can be so extreme that people avoid talking to strangers, even though doing so is likely to be an enjoyable experience.
sentences.translation: 参考译文按段定稿的整篇参考译文是复盘资产，考卷上只印英文原文——英语二英译汉满分 15 分，按「理解准确、表达通顺连贯、无错译漏译」整篇四档评分。

sentences.text: P3 During conversations with short gaps, people feel more connected to their conversation partners.
But such feelings of connection markedly dip when entering a long gap.
Long gaps between strangers are likely to be followed by a change in topic.
P4
But the opposite seems to be true for conversations between friends.
Long gaps there saw increased connection.
Between friends, longer gaps seem to provide natural moments for reflection and expression.
